title: board-from-events — a Servex-hosted agent appears on the board without anyone writing a card

set.request: Run log-model's fold for real: an Agents strip on /framework/ai/v/3/ fed live from Servex's /agents and /api/stream, and a landed minion/task-mastermind becomes a board card with no human writing it.
set.now: reading common.md, phases.md item 5, log-model's fold.js/events.md, and v/3's page.js/timeline.js/v3.css
steps: Read common.md, phases.md item 5, log-model's fold/events docs, v3 readme + page.js + timeline.js + v3.css, Servex.js/Stream.js/Agents.js/registry.js/tools.js
Confirm /agents and /api/stream lack CORS (curl -i) and add it in Servex.js, restart Servex
Build the Agents strip: a new v/3/agents.js module, wired into page.js under the head row, live off /agents + /api/stream, absent (not erroring) when Servex is down
Wire a stopped minion/task-mastermind's last transcript into a board card via Timeline's own card() merge, in the browser, never board.jsonl
Reload hold, node --check, headless load on a private port, release
Proof: spawn a real Haiku agent through Servex's MCP from a claude -p turn, screenshot the strip live and the landed card, then the Servex-down path with zero console errors
set.outcome:
**A Servex-hosted agent now appears on the AI board with nobody writing a card for it.** An Agents strip sits under the toolbar on every view of `/framework/ai/v/3/` — one chip per live Claude session Servex is holding, pushed the instant a token arrives over `GET /api/stream` (never polled), absent with zero errors when Servex is not running. Click a chip and its live transcript opens. When a `minion` or `task-mastermind` is stopped, its own last words become a real board card — folded in the browser from its own log, merged the same way any `board.jsonl` line is, never written to `board.jsonl` itself.

**Proven with a real agent, not a mock.** Spawned three Haiku sessions through Servex's MCP from separate `claude -p --strict-mcp-config` turns, each counting to thirty. [`shots/strip-live.png`](shots/strip-live.png) shows the strip live mid-count; after `stop_agent`, the grid view's own "N left" counter moved 97 → 98 in the same open page with no reload — [`shots/card-landed.png`](shots/card-landed.png). [`shots/servex-down.png`](shots/servex-down.png) shows the board loading normally with the strip absent when pointed at a dead port — one unavoidable browser-level network diagnostic (`Failed to load resource`, confirmed on a blank test page too, independent of any JS catch), zero errors thrown or logged by this code.

**Fixed a real bug found live:** the strip's first version rebuilt every row on every token from every agent, which made a chip briefly unclickable under real concurrent load — now it only rebuilds when who is live actually changes. **`GET /agents` and `GET /api/stream` had no CORS** (would have silently failed from the site's own origin) — fixed in `Servex/Servex.js`, Servex restarted and confirmed alive.

**Left named, not fixed:** the deep link `/framework/ai/v/3/` double-mounts the whole page (a pre-existing catalog-plus-leaf quirk, unrelated to this task, doubling every top-level fetch it makes) — proof screenshots use `/framework/ai/` instead, which mounts once. `Servex/Servex.js`'s own loopback guard never actually gates `GET /api/stream` (registered before `guard()` runs) — a pre-existing gap, out of this task's CORS-only fence.
